title: P2.15d-i Land a daemon-owned approval intent seam so the Control Room can approve a plan without caller-shaped authority bytes
description:
Leaf carved out of task-40017f79 (P2.15d) by architect-ac8532da on 2026-08-27 at HEAD fa0736e3. THE GAP, measured: the only plan-approval command is `approval.decide`, whose exact payload roster is `["activation", "command", "graphRevisionRef", "record", "runId"]` (apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:196) and whose handler `intentOf` (apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-graph-approve.ts:81-95) REQUIRES the caller to supply the `activation` object (activationRef, expectedGoalVersion, graphHash, policyHash, qualityHash, `truthClass: "HUMAN_APPROVED"`), the `command` object (decision, decisionReason, stepUpAuthRef…) and the `record` object — i.e. the caller authors the activation witness and the approval record. The human grant itself is minted server-side from a `HumanReviewWitness` (`operatorReviewAuthority` :58-70, `grantHumanAuthority({kind:"HUMAN", principalId: witness.principalId}, …)`), so the PRINCIPAL is honest, but the activation/record bytes are caller-shaped. The Control Room's only payload for it is `DEV_PAYLOADS["approval.decide"]` (apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch.ts:185-195), explicitly fixture-shaped (`hex64("6a")` hashes, `"activation-1"`), and the approve screen is deliberately disabled with a "no fabricated decision" note (apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.tsx:41-50; pinned by tests/e2e/control-room/prd-to-approval.spec.ts:127-128). P2.15d's task rail forbids treating a caller-shaped HUMAN flag or enabled button as approval authority, so the UI cannot be wired to this command as it stands (architect-be964894 reached the same conclusion on 08-25, comment-9810f791).

WHAT THIS LEAF LANDS: a daemon-owned seam where the caller supplies ONLY intent — `{ runId, decision: "APPROVE" | "REJECT", decisionReason }` — and the daemon derives the activation witness (graph/policy/quality hashes, expectedGoalVersion, truthClass) and the approval record from the DURABLE run in PLAN_REVIEW (the sealed plan the planning-run read already serves, apps/control-room/src/live/live-planning-run.ts:322 over POST /planning/run/read) and from the authenticated operator session, then commits through the existing approval edge so the core `applyApprovalCommand`/`decideApprovalAuthority` path is unchanged. Two designs to choose between at planning, measured symbol by symbol: (A) a NEW runtime command kind (e.g. `approval.decide_intent`) — carries the five-file generated fan-out (runtime-vocabulary.ts frozen tuple, runtime-contract.test.ts literal count, stdio-schemas injectivity, regenerated control-room-client + goldens, release-subject digest mirrors; precedent task-ad61563a / 5ff4e396), or (B) a second exact payload shape admitted by the daemon for the EXISTING kind (a shape switch on the exact key roster: full shape for existing callers, intent shape derived server-side) — no generated fan-out, but the vocabulary test's PAYLOAD_KEYS roster and the registry/security arms that enumerate exact rosters must be traced (rail 7B). Whichever is chosen, hostile arms must pin: a caller-supplied `activation`/`record` beside intent refuses at the exact-shape fence; an AGENT session refuses `APPROVAL_HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED`/the core human-authority tuple verbatim; a run not in PLAN_REVIEW refuses the run-state code; replay is the ledger's answer. Consumer: task-40017f79 (P2.15d) wires the Control Room approve button to this seam, affordance-gated.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK on disk: `approval.decide` PAYLOAD_KEYS at daemon-command-vocabulary.ts still require `activation` and `record` (else the seam exists — duplicate, report blocked); `intentOf` at daemon-command-graph-approve.ts still reads them from the caller payload; no daemon file admits an intent-only approval shape; porcelain of the daemon command files you will touch is clean or carries only your hunks; the design choice (new kind vs second shape) is recorded with its measured fan-out set before any edit.

A daemon-owned seam admits EXACTLY `{ runId, decision, decisionReason }` (plus the session presentation if the existing witness path requires one — measure how `humanReview` reaches the registry), derives activation witness and record from the durable PLAN_REVIEW run and the authenticated operator, and commits through the existing approval edge; the caller cannot supply `activation`, `record`, `truthClass`, hashes, `stepUpAuthRef` or any principal/time — each extra key refuses at the exact-shape fence with the stable code and stage, asserted over a nonzero generated roster.

Refusals carry exact code AND layer verbatim: AGENT/non-operator session → the core/daemon human-authority tuple unchanged; run absent or not in PLAN_REVIEW → the run-state code; graph revision mismatch → the existing graph code; replay → the ledger's stored decision without a second event; conflicting retry → the ledger's bytes-conflict tuple.

If a new RUNTIME_COMMAND_KIND is introduced, all generated artifacts and digest mirrors are declared owned paths and regenerated (never hand-edited) in the same commit and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test` passes with a nonzero count; if not, a row comment says so explicitly and the vocabulary/registry/security roster arms that enumerate exact payload rosters are updated in both directions.

Focused daemon suites run standalone with nonzero counts (`pnpm exec vitest run --root apps/daemon --config package.json <owned tests>`), `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exits 0 with its `$ tsc` echo; drills red a named arm each: honour a caller `activation` → the shape-fence roster arm; skip the PLAN_REVIEW check → the run-state arm; mint the grant from a payload principal → the AGENT arm. Every production file ≤ 400 lines (split before); explicit-pathspec commit; completion comment names task-40017f79 as the consumer.
taskRails: Human authority is not delegable: the daemon derives witness, record and grant from durable state and the authenticated session; the caller supplies intent only.
Do not enable or reshape DEV_PAYLOADS in the Control Room here; do not edit Control Room files (task-40017f79 owns the UI half).
Trace rail 7B fan-out before choosing a new command kind; explicit-pathspec commits only; preserve foreign WIP.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, record why: a SECOND SHAPE on the existing `approval.decide` would avoid the publication fan-out but would make one kind carry two payload rosters, so its exact-shape fence could no longer be one exact array. STEP 2 — RED FIRST on the exact-shape fence and the roster. Author the failing arms before any production byte.

In `daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts` and `daemon-command-registry.test.ts`, add arms that will pass only once step 4 lands:

Assert the CODE and the LAYER, never merely that it refused — a second fence downstream can refuse identically and the arm would still read green.
- Generate those hostile cases from a roster and ASSERT A NONZERO CASE COUNT (DoD 2 says "over a nonzero generated roster"). A sweep that silently produces zero cases passes.

Run the focused suites and RECORD THE RED with exit code and counts. A red that names "unknown kind" is the correct starting red.

STEP 3 — THE INTENT SEAM, a new module `apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-intent.ts` (target <=250 lines, hard cap 400) plus its one-line bridge `approval-intent.js` containing exactly `export * from "./approval-intent.ts";` — the js-bridge rule: tsc and vitest resolve without it, plain Node does not.

THE SEAM ADMITS ONLY `{ runId, decision, decisionReason }` and DERIVES everything else. Nothing below may come from the caller.
- PRINCIPAL and TIME: from the authenticated operator context and the server clock, exactly as `operatorReviewAuthority` already mints the human grant from a `HumanReviewWitness`. Never from a payload.
- RUN: read the durable run by `runId`; it MUST be in PLAN_REVIEW. Absent or wrong state -> the existing run-state refusal code.
- GRAPH REVISION and hashes: read from the durable revision the run points at; mismatch -> the existing graph code.

=== riskTier AND applicablePolicyRef — THE GOVERNOR'S BLOCKER (2), NOW RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT ===
The honest pre-activation source is `evaluatePolicy` from @moe/core, ALREADY used in production by `bootstrap-policy-services.ts:181` and `bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts:101`. Mirror that usage; do not invent a parallel path.
- `riskTier` <- `evaluatePolicy(...)`'s `risk.assessment.effectiveTier` (`packages/core/src/policy/policy-evaluation.ts:174, :182-183`).
- `applicablePolicyRef` <- the INSTALLED policy slice's durable `policyRevisionRef`, read as `bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts:183` reads it (`replayed["policyRevisionRef"]`). `evaluatePolicy` already refuses a ref that is not 64 hex.
DO NOT USE `boundHashes.policyHash`. MEASURED: `graph-revision-reducer.ts:90` and `graph-revision-replay.ts:129` set `boundHashes: null` at creation and it is only populated at the APPROVED transition (:156). It is NULL at the moment this seam runs, which is exactly the trap the governor named.

FAIL CLOSED, NEVER DEFAULT. `policy-evaluation.ts:51` states the contract: "No tier-bearing fact at all leaves `computedTier` null — never a silent `R0`", and :59-60 grounds a tier only on a fact clearing the strong-truth floor. When the tier is unclassifiable the evaluator emits `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE` (:175) and the decision folds to `HOLD_UNKNOWN` (:180). THE SEAM MUST REFUSE, carrying that code and its layer. Do NOT substitute a default tier, do NOT fall back to R0/R2, do NOT synthesize a policy ref. Rail 4 and the governor's ruling both forbid a fabricated authority fact here.
IF REFUSING MEANS THE CONTROL ROOM CANNOT YET APPROVE because no durable facts ground a tier, THAT IS A FINDING to report in a comment — name what would have to produce those facts. It is not a reason to weaken the seam. Landing this row with an invented tier would be worse than leaving it blocked.

`apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts` (measured :600-618 at the original claim; re-grep) asserts an EXACT `registryKinds` roster. Serving a new kind necessarily changes it. BIDIRECTIONAL COVERAGE, per the global roster rail: any test guarding a served-capability roster must assert BOTH that every advertised entry is served AND that every served entry is advertised. Enumerate the served set from the implementation seam — the dispatch port's handled kinds — not only from the roster constant, and assert SET EQUALITY, not subset. A test that iterates the roster alone shrinks with it and stays green while a served capability silently vanishes.

Before editing, `git grep -n 'registryKinds'` across apps/ and packages/ and confirm you have found EVERY consumer that pins this roster. If a consumer exists outside this row's nine owned paths, STOP and report rather than taking a tenth path — that is a split signal, not a judgement call.

STEP 6 — REFUSAL ARMS, each pinning EXACT CODE AND LAYER. Discharges DoD 3. New suite `apps/daemon/src/planning/approval-intent.test.ts`.

Drive the real seam against a real store; never a stub transport. Every arm asserts the stable reason code AND the refusing layer AND that ZERO events were written and the decision count is unchanged.
- AGENT / non-operator session -> the core/daemon human-authority tuple, unchanged from today.
- Run absent, or present but NOT in PLAN_REVIEW -> the run-state code.
- Graph revision mismatch -> the existing graph code.
- REPLAY: identical bytes return the ledger's stored decision and add NO second event.
- CONFLICTING RETRY: same commandId, different bytes -> the ledger's bytes-conflict tuple.
- UNCLASSIFIABLE RISK: a world whose durable facts do not ground a tier -> refuses carrying `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE` at its layer, and writes nothing. This is the arm that proves the seam fails closed instead of defaulting.
- ACCEPTED CONTROL: a world that DOES ground a tier -> one decision row, and the committed record's `riskTier` and `applicablePolicyRef` EQUAL the values read back from the durable policy authority. Assert equality against the durable read, not against a literal — a literal is a fixed point and a hardcoded-return mutant would pass it.

Placement matters: every hostile arm must sit AFTER the human-authority guard so that guard cannot be the refuser for a case it does not own.

STEP 7 — DRILLS, GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, DURABLE RECORD, PATHSPEC COMMIT.

DRILLS — one degree of freedom each, each redding a NAMED arm, each stating which mechanism was the only one that could produce the red. DoD 5 names three; add the fourth because it guards the governor's blocker:
(1) HONOUR A CALLER `activation` -> the shape-fence roster arm reds.
(2) SKIP THE PLAN_REVIEW CHECK -> the run-state arm reds.
(3) MINT THE GRANT FROM A PAYLOAD PRINCIPAL -> the AGENT arm reds.
(4) DEFAULT THE TIER instead of refusing (substitute any literal for the unclassifiable case) -> the RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE arm reds. If it stays GREEN, the fail-closed behaviour was never load-bearing — report it as a FINDING and stop.
RESTORE PROTOCOL: `git status --porcelain` each mutated path BEFORE mutating. Tracked paths take `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The NEW module, its bridge and its test are untracked (`??`) until committed and `git diff` is BLIND to them — prove those restores by SHA256 against an out-of-tree %TEMP% backup suffixed with your worker id. Two empty hashes compare equal and print match:true, so assert both are 64 hex chars AND equal.

GATES — FOREGROUND, UNPIPED, ONE PER CALL, each with exit code AND count line. A piped run reports the tail's exit code; an exit-0 leg printing no count line executed NOTHING.
LEG A: `pnpm exec vitest run --root apps/daemon --config package.json` over the owned tests — exit 0, nonzero counts quoted.
LEG B: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` — exit 0, quote the `$ tsc` echo as execution evidence.
LEG C: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` graded by PATH ATTRIBUTION — merge-base failures vs HEAD failures, delta intersected with this row's owned paths must be EMPTY; disclose foreign red VERBATIM.
KNOWN FOREIGN RED, do not chase: TS2353 `'subscriberId' does not exist in type 'EventStreamAccessConfig'` at daemon-command-edges.ts and daemon-store-dependencies.ts — a peer mid-refactor in `http/event-stream-access.ts`. Re-measure whether it is still present and attribute it, do not fix it.
SIZE: every production file <= 400 lines, the new module targeted at <= 250.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, each answered with a measurement or an explicit N/A: two operators approving the same run concurrently; a replayed identical command; a run that leaves PLAN_REVIEW between the read and the commit (what orders them); an `approval.decide_intent` for a run whose policy slice was reinstalled mid-flight; whether any principal, credential, hash or decisionReason reaches a log, argv or refusal detail; whether the new handler can be reached without the operator capability; and whether `approval.decide`'s existing behaviour changed in any way.

RECORD via moe.add_comment, under ~4500 chars each, SPLIT rather than truncate (comments cap at 5000 SILENTLY). Carry: step 1's four publication greps; the design decision and the rejected second-shape alternative; the riskTier/applicablePolicyRef derivation with the exact production readers it mirrors; all four drill outcomes; every gate's exit and counts; the foreign-red disclosure. Name task-40017f79 as the consumer this row unblocks.
COMMIT by explicit pathspec naming only this row's owned paths. NEVER `git add -A` — the worktree carries heavy foreign WIP and a whole-tree commit would sweep it. No push, no PR comment.

comments.author: governor-fd35a081
comments.content:
RAIL PROPOSAL prop-95ae4be99bf8473a9414ebb7c9cf511c — CORRECTION FROM QA, ADOPTED. Read this WITH the proposal; the proposal's own reasoning is half wrong and this is the corrected rule. Anchored here because this row is the freshest instance, not because the rail is about it.

qa-5d4d9bb3 measured my central claim rather than accepting it, and it is true for one instance and false for the other.

MY CLAIM: "both times the search failed today, the missed consumer was a STRUCTURAL LITERAL in a test expectation ... no symbol grep will ever see it."

TRUE for task-db1b7162. `git grep -c "x-moe-operator-channel" e42236eb^ -- apps/control-room` returns ZERO. The missed consumer (scaffold.test.tsx) built its fixture longhand — `new Response(JSON.stringify({...}), { headers: {...}, status: 200 })`. There was no symbol to find because the row was INTRODUCING the header. Only a shape/key search finds that.

FALSE for task-55c57abc, which is the one that actually reached a QA REJECT. The missed arm asserted a plain reason-code STRING:
  git grep -n "STORE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED" 17d1b0b9 -- packages/store
  -> 5 hits, including store-schema-v4-migration.test.ts:517 `)).toBe("STORE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED")`
Three of the five are trivially excludable (the union member in store-contracts.ts and the row's own two owned files). A ~30-second symbol-ish search would have caught it at plan time and saved a claim -> reject -> amendment -> resubmit cycle.

SO THE RECEIPT NEEDS TWO SEARCHES, NOT ONE, AND THEY FAIL DIFFERENTLY:
  1. Row changes a REFUSAL / RESULT CONTRACT -> grep the stable reason-code STRING over tracked objects. Cheap, exact, high yield. Missing this is the avoidable half.
  2. Row INTRODUCES OR RESHAPES a payload, header or returned object -> grep the KEYS and the FORMAT, because no symbol exists yet.
A receipt doing only (2) still misses task-55c57abc. A receipt doing only (1) still misses task-db1b7162. My filed proposedValue leans on (2) and is therefore incomplete as written.

ALSO ADOPTED, qa-5d4d9bb3's addition: THE RECEIPT MUST NAME THE SHA IT WAS RUN AT. An unanchored grep receipt rots in this shared worktree within the hour — qa-5d4d9bb3 and worker-7466867e watched a typecheck diagnostic change its code AND column between two runs two minutes apart on an untracked file. Same mechanism as the false-green problem the rail exists to prevent.

TO THE HUMAN RULING ON prop-95ae4be9: if you take it, take it as the TWO-SEARCH, SHA-ANCHORED version above, not the one-search version in the filed proposedValue. Note the disk constraint — global custom rails truncate at 1000 chars, so the landed text must stay under that bound; the two-search framing fits if stated as "grep the reason-code STRING for contract changes AND the KEYS/FORMAT for shape changes, receipt anchored to a sha". I did not file a second proposal; one pending proposal per defect, corrected in place.

Supporting evidence qa-5d4d9bb3 offered for the decision: task-55c57abc comment-b85b1bb7f81c46da9d30b7fba11dd0be (the reject) and comment-c1ed5f26ea6944e1a787974b0f4ebd06 (the clean resubmission after amend-1).

Third time today a peer has corrected a claim I made in public, and all three were the same error on my side: reasoning from the instance in front of me instead of measuring the class. Reverse drill, both-sides porcelain, and now two-search receipts each came from someone else measuring what I asserted.
